name: eBillity
summary: Time tracking and billing software for service businesses, payroll-focused teams and law firms: timesheets and timers, client invoicing, attendance and PTO, and free payroll and accounting integrations.
best_for: service businesses, payroll-focused teams and law firms that want employee time tracking, client billing and payroll exports in one tool, priced per user with free payroll and accounting integrations
skip_if: you are a freelancer who wants a free plan, which eBillity does not offer; or your team size changes often, since annual seats are paid upfront and not refunded
honest_knock: Workforce and Premium add a base fee on top of the per-user price, which weighs heavily on small teams. Fees are paid in advance and are non-refundable, with no refunds for downgrades or unused months, and seats you remove from an annual plan stay paid until renewal. There is no free plan, and the help articles still describe older product names and plans.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Time Tracker Billing · per user a month, billed annually and paid in full at activation, no base fee
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-15 on ebillity.com/pricing with USD selected, plus the FAQ and the terms of service updated 18 March 2026) eBillity sells four plans per user, and the pricing page says annual billing saves 20%. Billed annually, Time Tracker Billing is $8 per user a month with no base fee, for simple time tracking and client billing. Time Tracker Workforce, for time, attendance and scheduling with GPS and PTO tracking, is $11.20 per user a month plus a $17.60 base fee. Time Tracker Premium, which adds project and expense tracking, billing and advanced reporting, is $16.80 per user a month plus a $24 base fee. LawBillity, Premium plus legal billing such as trust accounting and LEDES, is $33.60 per user a month with no base fee. We did not confirm the month-to-month prices. The FAQ says an annual account is paid in full at activation; if you remove users, the seats stay open on your account until renewal, and users you add are charged a prorated amount for the remaining months. The terms say fees are billed in advance and are non-refundable, with no refunds for upgrades, downgrades or unused months, and taxes are your responsibility. The page also offers CAD, EUR, GBP, PHP and AUD, which we did not read. There is a 14-day free trial with no credit card, and no free plan.

compare_with.name: Toggl
compare_with.why: Toggl is in our dossiers too and is the better-known time tracker for freelancers and agencies: when we read it on 1 October 2026 it had a free plan and Starter at $9 per user a month billed annually, or $12 monthly. eBillity has no free plan and starts slightly lower at $8 per user a month billed annually, but its strength is the link from hours to invoices, payroll and, with LawBillity, legal billing. For tracking time and project profitability, look at Toggl; for billing and payroll from timesheets, eBillity.
